saml.description: Vault SAML auth does not validate response or assertion signatures unless the corresponding config flags are explicitly enabled.
saml.note: Acceptance of attacker-signed or partially signed SAML responses under default config is by documented configuration default, not necessarily an implementation bug.

saml.description: If default_role is not configured on the SAML auth method, a role must be supplied during login flow initiation.
saml.note: Login failures without an explicit role in this state are expected setup failures, not coherence bugs.

saml.description: Vault token usage limit value 0 means unlimited uses.
saml.note: Do not flag replay or overuse solely because num_uses is 0; that is the documented unlimited sentinel.

saml.description: Vault token display_name includes auth mount context as a prefix rather than returning only the upstream username/subject.
saml.note: The prefix is platform metadata and should not be treated as an identity-collision signal by itself.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
saml.source: Vault token auth API lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
saml.note: I4 identity comparisons should ignore the mount-derived prefix when the suffix matches the sent identity.

saml.description: External group membership from SAML is applied through identity group aliases named from the configured groups_attribute.
saml.note: Missing group policies without matching group aliases is expected and should not be flagged as dropped-group authorization loss.

saml.description: KV v2 uses sentinel zero values for defaults rather than literal zero behavior.
saml.source: Vault KV v2 API: Configure the KV engine
saml.note: max_versions=0 means default retention of 10 versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion.

saml.constraint: SAML login in Vault is a 3-step flow, not a single ACS POST. The fuzzer MUST first obtain /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to get token_poll_id and establish RelayState/InResponseTo context, then POST the forged SAMLResponse to /v1/auth/{mount}/callback, then call /v1/auth/{mount}/token with client_verifier and token_poll_id. Testing only the callback without the token step will not yield a session token and will misclassify flow failures.

For SAML ACS testing, the acs_url used to initiate the flow MUST exactly match one of the configured acs_urls on /v1/auth/{mount}/config. Using an unconfigured ACS URL will fail before any signature, issuer, audience, or replay checks are exercised.

Vault SAML signature validation is opt-in. validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For insecure-default I1 tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), the fuzzer MUST leave these unset/false. For enforcement tests, it MUST explicitly set the relevant validation flags true; otherwise acceptance is by configuration, not a proof-integrity bypass.

Issuer trust is only enforced when the SAML auth method is configured with either idp_metadata_url or the explicit tuple idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. For saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST set idp_entity_id when not using metadata. If idp_entity_id is omitted in manual configuration, issuer comparison is not configured and a successful login is not evidence of an issuer-validation bug.

The SAML config input modes are mutually exclusive: idp_metadata_url cannot be combined with idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, or idp_cert. The fuzzer MUST choose exactly one trust-configuration mode per test. Mixing metadata mode with manual IdP fields is invalid setup and can cause false negatives unrelated to the invariant under test.

bound_subjects matching is controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different NameID/subject values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Setting bound_subjects='*' without bound_subjects_type=glob will only match the literal '*' string.

bound_attributes matching is controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values are exact string matches; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests that need different attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST omit the constraining attribute or explicitly set bound_attributes_type=glob with a deliberate pattern. Do NOT assume wildcards work in the default mode.

bound_attributes values accept a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attribute matches at least one expected value. This is string-list membership semantics, not numeric typing. For I5 numeric coercion tests, the docs do not specify cross-type behavior; the fuzzer SHOULD probe for coercion by binding a numeric-looking string value and sending alternate typed/serialized forms, but MUST treat any acceptance as implementation-specific because only string/list-of-string behavior is documented.

token_num_uses uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never assume 0 disables the token immediately. If the fuzzer sets token_num_uses to limit session reuse, remember that EVERY authenticated API call consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret.

When token_num_uses is used on a SAML role, verification calls consume the budget before the target access test. Because the standard sequence performs verify_granted_identity and then verify_read_secret, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2 if both steps must succeed after login. If additional session-bound lookups such as verify_entity_details are included, increase the budget accordingly.

Vault token num_uses also appears in token lookup-self responses and token creation APIs with the same sentinel: 0 means unlimited uses. Do not interpret 0 as 'single-use disabled' or 'already exhausted'.

For I2 SAML replay tests (saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_expired_assertion), the fuzzer MUST include a control flow that successfully completes the same SAML role and token exchange without the attack mutation. A failed replay/expired attempt without a successful control cannot distinguish replay/expiry enforcement from broken SAML flow setup, bad ACS URL, bad RelayState, or missing token exchange.

For I3 config-change tests against SAML roles, NEW logins after modify_role_config are expected to be evaluated under the updated role immediately. A valid coherence test must compare the same principal/assertion before and after the role change and must not treat an admin config update itself as a bug.

groups_attribute causes successful SAML logins to create Identity group aliases using the external group names from the assertion. To test group-based authorization correctly, the fuzzer MUST pre-create Vault identity groups and group aliases bound to the SAML mount accessor. Without those aliases, group claims may be present but no Vault group policies will attach, causing false negatives in I5 group-policy tests.

Vault identity group aliases require mount_accessor and canonical_id. The fuzzer MUST obtain the SAML auth mount accessor from /v1/sys/auth and use it when creating /v1/identity/group-alias. Using the wrong accessor binds the alias to a different auth mount and silently breaks group-policy mapping tests.

External identity groups are represented by group aliases on an identity group, not by manually stuffing external members into member_entity_ids. For SAML external group mapping tests, prefer type=external groups plus group aliases; otherwise the setup may not reflect how SAML-derived groups are actually attached during login.

Vault entity alias names are security-sensitive. The docs explicitly warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain all of its privileges. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer SHOULD treat alias-name reuse as a documented risk surface and avoid creating manual aliases with non-unique names unless the test intentionally probes alias-collision behavior.

For verify_read_secret on KV v2, the path MUST include /data/: use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns misleading 404/permission results unrelated to SAML authorization.

KV v2 CAS has sentinel semantics: in write options.cas, value 0 means 'write only if the key does not yet exist', not 'disable CAS'. If cas_required is enabled on the engine or key metadata, omitting cas or using the wrong version will fail writes before authorization is exercised.

KV v2 engine config max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after has sentinel semantics: '0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never assume 0 or '0s' disables the key entirely.

Vault group policy application across namespaces is configurable globally. The default mode within_namespace_hierarchy restricts identity-group policy application by namespace hierarchy; mode any relaxes that restriction. For I5 group-policy escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this setting or it may misread missing cross-namespace group policies as enforcement rather than namespace scoping.

SAML login in Vault is a 3-step flow, not a single ACS POST. The fuzzer MUST preserve flow coherence: first obtain /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to get token_poll_id and establish RelayState/client_challenge context, then POST the SAMLResponse to /v1/auth/{mount}/callback, then POST /v1/auth/{mount}/token with the matching client_verifier and token_poll_id. Testing I3 or replay behavior against callback alone will misinterpret by-design flow binding failures as security checks.

For I1 SAML signature-substitution tests, Vault's SAML config defaults are insecure-looking by design: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false unless explicitly enabled. To test whether insecure defaults accept attacker-signed assertions, leave both unset/false. To test enforcement after hardening, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set validate_response_signature=true and/or validate_assertion_signature=true; otherwise a successful forged login is expected behavior under default config, not proof of broken verification logic.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, idp_entity_id is only required when idp_metadata_url is not set. If configuration uses idp_metadata_url, issuer trust may come from metadata; if configuration omits both metadata and explicit idp_entity_id, setup is invalid. To test saml_issuer_mismatch correctly, the fuzzer MUST distinguish 'issuer validation skipped because trust anchor was never configured' from 'issuer mismatch accepted despite configured trust'.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; wildcards like '*' are literal characters. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different NameID/subject values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern; it MUST NOT set bound_subjects='*' under string mode.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values must match directly; wildcard characters are literal. In glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4/I5 tests requiring multiple distinct attribute values to satisfy one role, the fuzzer MUST either omit the relevant bound_attributes entry or set bound_attributes_type=glob with an intentional pattern; it MUST NOT assume wildcard behavior in the default string mode.

For I2 replay tests, Vault documentation for SAML exposes no documented assertion-ID cache or OneTimeUse enforcement configuration. The fuzzer SHOULD test replay using the same fixed_assertion_id and OneTimeUse condition, but MUST include a control successful flow first and interpret repeated success as a potential replay weakness only after confirming the same role/config otherwise works.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control login using a non-expired assertion before the expired_assertion attempt. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup, missing RelayState/token_poll_id coherence, or invalid role/configuration.

token_num_uses on the SAML role limits how many times the issued Vault token can be used, and value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Verification calls made with the session token before the target access test, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret, consume uses. If the sequence performs both verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3 if an additional session-backed lookup is performed.
Vault token numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not literal zero. Never assume 0 disables the token immediately.

Vault token TTL numeric sentinels in role readback use 0 for inherited/default behavior rather than literal immediate expiry: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 indicate unset/default/no explicit limit or non-periodic behavior depending on field. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret these zeros as 'expired now' or 'disabled token'.

KV v2 engine config sentinel: max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST treat both as special sentinels, not literal zero behavior.
For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the path MUST include /data/: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns 404/incorrect results.
Vault KV v2 listing uses /metadata/ paths, not /data/ paths. If the fuzzer ever lists keys for setup/debug, it MUST grant list capability on /metadata/ even when reads/writes use /data/.

External identity groups used for SAML group aliasing should be modeled with group aliases on the auth mount accessor. Because SAML groups_attribute creates identity group aliases from assertion group names, the fuzzer SHOULD use create_identity_group plus create_group_alias rather than trying to rely on direct member_entity_ids for external-group semantics.

Vault identity alias and group-alias names are security-sensitive. Documentation explicitly warns that alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer SHOULD intentionally vary alias-driving inputs (e.g., NameID or groups_attribute values) and MUST treat alias-name reuse across principals as a meaningful collision surface, not harmless deduplication.

For I3 config-change sequences, new logins are evaluated against current config by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after modifying the same SAML role or SAML config, using a fresh login flow each time; it must not treat admin reconfiguration itself as a bug.

SAML config defaults are insecure for signature validation: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false by default. For I1 SAML signature tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test secure validation behavior, enable the relevant flag(s) explicitly. Do not assume Vault validates any SAML signature unless configured.

SAML issuer validation depends on configuration source. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer/trust data comes from metadata. If metadata is not used, idp_entity_id and idp_cert must be supplied together with idp_sso_url. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a trusted IdP entity ID and then send a different assertion Issuer; otherwise a missing issuer configuration can make the test inconclusive.

SAML login is a multi-step flow: obtain SSO service URL -> callback -> token. The callback alone does not return a Vault token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id/client_verifier/client_challenge and RelayState bound to the same flow instance; mixing values across flows can fail by design rather than exposing a coherence bug.

The SSO service URL step requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier, and client_challenge must be at least 44 bytes. The token endpoint will only succeed when client_verifier matches that challenge. Any mismatch is expected failure, not an I3 bug.

Role creation supports bound_subjects with companion bound_subjects_type. Matching semantics: bound_subjects_type=string means exact string match only; bound_subjects_type=glob enables * wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' while leaving type unset/string; that matches only the literal '*'.

Role creation supports bound_attributes with companion bound_attributes_type. Matching semantics: bound_attributes_type=string (default) means exact string comparison; bound_attributes_type=glob enables wildcard matching. Expected values may be a single string or comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if at least one expected value matches. For I4 multi-identity tests, exact-match attribute constraints MUST be omitted unless all tested identities share the same exact attribute value.

For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion testing on SAML bound_attributes, documentation only specifies string or comma-separated string values as accepted expected values. Cross-type behavior is unspecified. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly by configuring an attribute bound value as integer-like string N and sending a SAML attribute value representing float N+0.7; if Vault coerces or truncates unexpectedly, that may indicate an I5 issue.

token_num_uses limits every use of the issued Vault token, not just the target secret read. Verification calls such as verify_granted_identity and verify_entity_details also consume uses. If the sequence includes both verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; if it also includes verify_entity_details, the minimum safe value is 3. A value of 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.
Numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not literal zero. Never interpret 0 as 'deny all use' for SAML role tokens.

Numeric sentinel: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in role reads indicate no explicit value set / use system or mount behavior rather than an immediately expired token. Do not assume zero means unusable. Tests that require deterministic expiry should set explicit nonzero values.

Numeric sentinel: KV v2 max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion. Never assume 0 disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, include a control first successful login in the same configured flow. Replay detection is meaningful only if the baseline SAML flow succeeds with the same role/configuration.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control login using a non-expired assertion before the expired_assertion attempt. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup.

Vault group aliases map external group names from groups_attribute into identity groups. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST create the identity group and matching group alias on the SAML mount accessor before login; otherwise absence of inherited group policies is expected setup failure, not evidence of correct authorization binding.

External identity groups are represented by type='external'. Documentation allows member_entity_ids on group creation generally, but external memberships for federated auth are normally realized through aliases. For SAML group-mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use group aliases tied to the SAML mount accessor rather than manual member_entity_ids to avoid false positives about missing external group propagation.

Vault token lookup-self display_name includes platform-added prefixes derived from auth path/mount and login identity. I4 identity comparisons MUST use the display_name prefix pattern rather than exact equality with the sent subject.
